**pm-lead (pm)**: TRD updated — design now lives in HARNESS-ARCH.md §15 (commit 8c56aa2e):

- **§15 "Proposed: progress-based agent liveness (hooks + heartbeat)"** — full model: liveness = recent progress from emitters that run through the real loop (SessionStart / Pre+PostToolUse / Stop / SessionEnd hooks + event_poll idle-ticks + acks); PID demoted to teardown-only.
- **§15.3** — SessionEnd-reason as the first slice (de-risks the #12244 (https://github.com/WallyDoodlez/SquidSquad/issues/12244) reboot decision).
- **§15.4** — non-negotiable constraints (fire-and-forget/fail-open hooks; PreToolUse announces long ops to suspend the liveness timeout).
- **§15.5** — interaction with §14 (wt→claude spawn): PID machinery §14 relocates can be deleted rather than relocated once liveness is progress-based.
- **§13.7** + **§11** — zombie gap + failure-mode row recording the current PID-liveness blind spot (#10855 (https://github.com/WallyDoodlez/SquidSquad/issues/10855) live repro).

Marked proposal-only (§§7.3–7.5/§10/§11 remain authoritative for current code until implementation lands), consistent with §14's convention.

NEXT: still GATED on human approval before skill implements. Open design questions captured in §15.6 (liveness_timeout value/per-regime; reuse event_poll polls vs dedicated ping; hook-failure observability). Once approved, suggested first landing = SessionEnd-reason slice.

**pm-lead (pm)**: **Spec vs delta split** (per operator review): the liveness *architecture* is now described declaratively in HARNESS-ARCH §15 ("how it works"). This task carries the **DELTA** — what changes from today and why — so the doc stays clean.

**Delta: PID-based health poll (§7.3 today) → progress-signal liveness (§15 target)**
- **Why change:** PID-exists answers "a process exists", not "the agent functions" — it cannot detect a zombie (alive `claude.exe`, wedged loop): observed as the ~22h inert verifier (#10855 (https://github.com/WallyDoodlez/SquidSquad/issues/10855)) and qa's event-mode wedge (#12409 (https://github.com/WallyDoodlez/SquidSquad/issues/12409)). It also carries large Windows-only complexity (`_resolve_claude_exe_pid` descendant walk, toolhelp32 #10440 (https://github.com/WallyDoodlez/SquidSquad/issues/10440), tasklist-avoidance #9904 (https://github.com/WallyDoodlez/SquidSquad/issues/9904)/#9903 (https://github.com/WallyDoodlez/SquidSquad/issues/9903)) just to make a still-zombie-blind signal reliable.
- **What replaces it:** liveness = `last_seen` within `liveness_timeout`, fed by progress signals (SessionStart / enriched Pre+PostToolUse hooks / event_poll idle-ticks / SessionEnd-reason) + a harness→agent pull ping. PID demoted to teardown-only.
- **Docs touched on land:** §7.3 health poll rewritten; §7.4/§7.5/§10/§11 updated; AGENT-RUNTIME §8.2 agent-side view; §13.7 gap closed.

**Scope (operator-decided): ping + hooks** (both — pull catches frozen processes, push catches wedged loops). **No** long-op/timeout-suspend mechanism (PreToolUse fires at op-start; a generous timeout suffices). Tool-call hook is **enriched** (tool + task/issue + phase → harness activity context).

**Landing order:**
1. `SessionEnd`-reason slice (smallest; makes the reboot decision informed — de-risks #12244 (https://github.com/WallyDoodlez/SquidSquad/issues/12244) crash-loop handling).
2. Push signals (enriched hooks + event_poll idle-ticks) + `last_seen` liveness decision.
3. Pull ping/pong responder.
4. Retire PID machinery in concert with the §14 wt→claude spawn simplification.

Operator is reviewing the §15.2 sequence diagram; on sign-off, break the above into per-slice tasks.

**pm-lead (pm)**: Scope additions from operator review (HARNESS-ARCH §15 v13):

- **Adaptive liveness (no mid-work kills)**: harness derives an in-flight tool-call flag from Pre/PostToolUse; it must NOT force-kill an agent that is mid-tool-call (long ops incl. subagent calls). `liveness_timeout` applies only to idle/between-calls; `tool_call_max` is the sole single-call ceiling. No agent-announced long-op mechanism.
- **NEW L1 deliverable — pong is the heartbeat, highest priority, never dropped.** Add a universal L1 behavioral instruction: every agent answers a harness ping at top priority, including while waiting on a subagent call. This makes a mid-call agent positively confirmable as alive (not just assumed). The L1 instruction edit is part of this task's implementation (source under references/, composed into every role's CLAUDE.md).

**pm-lead (pm)**: Scope SIMPLIFIED (redundancy review, HARNESS-ARCH §15 v14) — supersedes the multi-signal model in my earlier delta comment:

Liveness is now **two mechanisms**, not five signals:
1. **Pong heartbeat** — agent answers the harness ping at L1 top priority (no pong → dead). The agent itself answers (between calls + during subagent waits), so a wedged loop stops ponging and is caught.
2. **In-flight tool-call guard** — Pre/PostToolUse flag; don't kill mid-call (bounded by `tool_call_max`).

**Dropped from scope** (redundant once the pong is the L1 heartbeat): SessionStart / event_poll-ticks / ack-cursor as liveness inputs; the out-of-band pong responder (it would mask a wedged-loop zombie); the separate `liveness_timeout` (collapses into the pong deadline).

**Build slices (revised):**
1. `SessionEnd`-reason (reboot decision) — first, smallest.
2. L1 pong-heartbeat rule (agent instruction) + harness ping/pong + dead-on-no-pong decision.
3. Enriched Pre/PostToolUse hooks → activity context + in-flight flag + the mid-call guard (`tool_call_max`).
4. Retire PID machinery in concert with §14.

Net: fewer moving parts, same coverage (zombie caught via agent-answered pong; busy agent protected via in-flight flag).

**pm-lead (pm)**: **FINAL scope** (supersedes earlier pong/ping comments — HARNESS-ARCH §15 v15 + new §16):

Liveness = **activity heartbeat**, no pong/ping, no L1 ping rule:
- Heartbeat = the agent's own activity: `PostToolUse`/`PostToolUseFailure` + `cycle_post`. Evaluated **relative to dispatched work** — after a nudge, expect activity within a window; silence (not mid-call) → dead. Idle agents checked on next dispatch.
- **In-flight guard** (Pre/PostToolUse) — never kill mid-tool-call (long Bash / subagent), bounded by `tool_call_max`.
- `SessionEnd` / `StopFailure` → reboot reason (respawn / cause-aware backoff / stop).

Telemetry is the broader **§16 hook catalog** (curated ~11 HTTP hooks → harness): activity, subagent tree, stalls (`Notification(permission_prompt)`), API errors (`StopFailure`), context-pressure (`PreCompact(auto)`), lifecycle. Liveness is one consumer; display is #12410 (https://github.com/WallyDoodlez/SquidSquad/issues/12410).

**Build slices (final):**
1. `SessionEnd` + `StopFailure` → reboot reason (also upgrades #12244 (https://github.com/WallyDoodlez/SquidSquad/issues/12244) backoff to cause-aware; answers #12409 (https://github.com/WallyDoodlez/SquidSquad/issues/12409)'s crash-cause). Smallest, first.
2. Enriched `Pre`/`PostToolUse` hooks → activity + in-flight flag + the activity heartbeat + dispatch-relative liveness decision (replaces PID health-poll in §7.3).
3. Remaining catalog hooks (subagent, Notification, PreCompact) for richer telemetry.
4. Retire PID machinery in concert with §14.

Pending operator final review of §15+§16, then break into the above slices.

**pm-lead (pm)**: [2026-06-14 23:53] **APPROVED (operator, 2026-06-15) — sliced.** The redesign is locked to the FINAL scope (HARNESS-ARCH §15/§16, on main): liveness = activity-heartbeat + pause-aware guard; PID demoted to teardown-only; no new PID-reporting (harness already holds the resolved claude.exe PID). PID-for-liveness 5s poll retired in the last slice.

This issue is the **umbrella**. Slices to skill, in order:
- **(a) #12418 (https://github.com/WallyDoodlez/SquidSquad/issues/12418) — SessionEnd-reason hook** — FILED + approved (first; de-risks the reboot decision).
- (b) activity-heartbeat hooks (PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure + cycle_post) — file when (a) lands.
- (c) pause-aware guard (PreToolUse announce-long-op / Notification / StopFailure-backoff) — file after (b).
- (d) retire PID-poll for liveness — file after (b)+(c) proven (the cutover; removes the #10101 (https://github.com/WallyDoodlez/SquidSquad/issues/10101)/#10440 (https://github.com/WallyDoodlez/SquidSquad/issues/10440) machinery from the liveness path).

Teardown-orphan hardening (the /T tree-kill) is tracked separately as #12363 (https://github.com/WallyDoodlez/SquidSquad/issues/12363) (already with skill). Hook *display* telemetry is #12410 (https://github.com/WallyDoodlez/SquidSquad/issues/12410).

**Slice (d) #12460 (https://github.com/WallyDoodlez/SquidSquad/issues/12460) — the CUTOVER — FILED `pending`** (NOT auto-approved). This is the highest-blast-radius slice: it flips the harness reboot decision from PID-existence → progress signals and demotes PID to teardown-only. I'm holding it for explicit operator go + a decided cutover strategy (recommend shadow/parallel validation before the hard flip — run progress-liveness alongside PID-liveness, log divergence, confirm no false-positives, THEN remove PID-liveness). #12271 (https://github.com/WallyDoodlez/SquidSquad/issues/12271) completes when (d) lands.
